savings_or_continuation_provisions.quote: Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect: (i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or (ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

The Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the heads of agencies shall promptly take steps to rescind any orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies, or portions thereof, implementing or enforcing the Executive Orders identified in section 2 of this order, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, including the Administrative Procedure Act, 5 U.S.C. 551 et seq. If in any case such rescission cannot be finalized immediately, the Director and the heads of agencies shall promptly take steps to provide all available exemptions authorized by any such orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law.

any personnel positions, committees, task forces, or other entities established pursuant to the Executive Orders identified in section 2 of this order, including the regulatory reform officer positions and regulatory reform task forces established by sections 2 and 3 of Executive Order 13777, shall be abolished, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law.

transfer_provisions.quote: any personnel positions, committees, task forces, or other entities established pursuant to the Executive Orders identified in section 2 of this order, including the regulatory reform officer positions and regulatory reform task forces established by sections 2 and 3 of Executive Order 13777, shall be abolished, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law.
transfer_provisions.note: Abolition wording, not a transfer: positions, committees, task forces and entities established under the six revoked orders (the order names the EO 13777 regulatory reform officer positions and task forces) 'shall be abolished, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law'. The order therefore treats those entities as surviving the revocation until abolished by agency action.

transfer_provisions.quote: The Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the heads of agencies shall promptly take steps to rescind any orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies, or portions thereof, implementing or enforcing the Executive Orders identified in section 2 of this order, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, including the Administrative Procedure Act, 5 U.S.C. 551 et seq. If in any case such rescission cannot be finalized immediately, the Director and the heads of agencies shall promptly take steps to provide all available exemptions authorized by any such orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law.
transfer_provisions.note: OMB and agency heads are told to rescind implementing orders, rules, regulations, guidelines and policies, and, where rescission cannot be finalized at once, to provide exemptions. Rules already issued under a revoked order are therefore treated as outliving the revocation until rescinded. No function is transferred to any successor.

exceptions.applies_to: No order in sec. 2 is excepted or partly revoked: all six (EO 13771, 13777, 13875, 13891, 13892, 13893) are revoked in one sentence without a proviso.

exceptions.quote: This order shall be implemented in a manner consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
exceptions.applies_to: Governs the sec. 3 implementation steps, not the sec. 2 revocation, which is self-executing.

effective_date_reading: The order states no effective date and has no delayed-effect wording (sec. 3 sets 'promptly' as the pace of implementation, which concerns rescission of implementing documents, not the revocation). It is dated 'The White House, January 20, 2021' and was printed January 25, 2021 (86 FR 7049). The OFR catalog notes on all six targets read 'Revoked by: EO 13992, January 20, 2021'. The revocations took effect on signing, 2021-01-20.
later_events_on_the_acting_order: EO 14148 sec. 2(g) (90 FR 8237, signed 2025-01-20) and EO 14154 (2025-01-20) revoke EO 13992 itself. Neither contains reinstatement wording (the held texts of EO 14148, 14154 and 14192 were searched for 'reinstat'; the only hits are in EO 14192 sec. 6(b) and (c), which reinstate OMB Circular A-4's 2003 version and a Treasury-OMB memorandum of agreement, not any order of this batch; EO 14192 sec. 3 re-creates a regulatory cap for fiscal year 2025 under its own authority and does not name EO 13771). A by-number scan of the 6,652 held Federal Register text files in jobs/fr-originals finds none of EO 13771, 13777, 13875, 13891, 13892, 13893 named by any order after EO 13992 as reinstated or revived. So the six sec. 2 revocations stand.
conclusion: EO 13992 (signed 2021-01-20, 86 FR 7049-7050, two pages, read once in full) revokes EO 13771, 13777, 13875, 13891, 13892 and 13893 in one sentence of sec. 2 ('are hereby revoked'). It states no effective date, so all six revocations took effect on signing, 2021-01-20. Sec. 3 orders OMB and agency heads to rescind implementing orders, rules, regulations, guidelines and policies and to abolish the personnel positions, committees, task forces and entities established under the revoked orders, expressly including the EO 13777 regulatory reform officer positions and task forces, 'as appropriate and consistent with applicable law'; this shows the drafters expected implementing documents and entities to survive until agency action, but it neither saves a revoked order nor delays the revocation. Sec. 4(a) is the usual non-impairment clause for statutory authority and OMB budget functions. No function is transferred to a successor, and no exception, pending-matter or transitional clause protects any of the six orders. The reader question for the batch is answered once here: all six are revoked whole on 2021-01-20, with an entity-survival and rule-survival consequence recorded per order in the savings residual.
